messages:
maya: heads-up: us-west-2 GPU pool sitting at ~92% and the short-chat model queue depth just spiked to 120. p50 latency is fine but p95 jumped to ~320ms. thinking about enabling cross-region spillover + model fallback for public traffic. any red flags (latency/regulatory/cost)?

sam: can you paste the recent metrics? queue depth over time, p50/p95, and how many requests are >200ms queued. also what is the current spillover policy (if any)?

maya: quick snapshot: queue_depth:120 (peak), p50:45ms, p95:320ms, ~18% requests waiting >200ms in the last 5m. current routing: region_preference: [us-west-2, us-east-1], spillover_enabled: false, fallback_models: [] (we relied on local autoscale so far).

kevin: for eu/reg customers we can't egress by default. we should gate cross-region spill to only non-EU tenants or those with consent. also think about tiers: priority customers (S2) should never spill or fallback to quantized models unless explicitly allowed.

rachel: agree on tiering. proposed soft strategy: S2 (priority) -> local only w/ higher admission thresholds; S1 (standard) -> allow cross-region spill up to a budgeted percent; Free tier -> aggressive fallback to smaller/quantized model or 429. admission control: start rejecting when per-pool queued_requests > 100 for standard traffic.

maya: that matches my instinct. curious about implementation details — do we do region spillover first or model fallback first? e.g., route to us-east-1 same model vs route to a quantized variant in us-west-2. Which preserves latency/cost best?

sam: it depends on SLOs. fallback order options: 1) cross-region same-model -> preserves model fidelity but increases egress/latency; 2) local quantized/model-smaller -> keeps latency but risks quality. suggest making this policy configurable per-route.

kevin: +1. also add a per-tenant budget check: if tenant has egress_budget_left < X then skip cross-region spill. we should record egress cost tag on traces so billing can reconcile.

rachel: here's a sample policy snippet (YAML) we can use in routing service for experiments:

```yaml
route: "/v1/generate"
priority_tiers:
  - name: S2
    allow_spill: false
    fallback_order: [local_same_model]
    admission_threshold: 200
  - name: S1
    allow_spill: true
    spill_budget_percent: 10
    fallback_order: [cross_region_same_model, local_quantized]
    admission_threshold: 100
  - name: free
    allow_spill: true
    spill_budget_percent: 25
    fallback_order: [local_quantized, reject]
    admission_threshold: 40
```

rachel: and operationally, add a circuit-breaker: if cross-region egress spikes cost > $C within window, flip spill to local-only for all S1 until manual review.

maya: nice. what about per-model admission/rate-limiter? short-chat has lots of tiny requests which are easy to batch but currently clog the scheduler.

sam: implement token-bucket per model_instance + queue_length cutoff. also we should add a "max_wait_ms" metadata on requests; if request waits > max_wait_ms we either run it on quantized model or 429. default max_wait_ms = 250ms for short-chat.

kevin: we also need visibility into where spilled requests go and success/failure histograms. instrumentation: add tags: origin_region, dest_region, fallback_used, tenant_tier, wait_ms, queue_pos. that will make postmortems easier.

ops-bot: alert: us-west-2 egress to us-east-1 increased by 82% in last 10m (threshold 50%)

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: routing/spillover/v0.1 -> staging at 1742016842 by rachel

sam: let's run the staging canary with 5% traffic from a non-EU test tenant and force fallback_order = [cross_region_same_model] so we can measure end-to-end latency/cost. canary window 10m.

maya: ok I'll carve out traffic and set the canary flag. will watch p95 and egress cost. also will add tenant exclusion for EU and S2.

kevin: one more thought: for cold-cache model variants (quantized), warm-up latency can be high. recommend pre-warm small pools if we plan to fallback to them frequently.

rachel: agreed. action items: (1) staging canary of spillover v0.1 (rachel/maya) (2) add per-tenant egress budget check (kevin) (3) instrument fallback tags + cost tracing (sam) (4) implement token-bucket + max_wait_ms for short-chat (rachel/ops). I'll allocate time on runway tonight to push the staging config. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — starting canary now. will post quick results in 10m. :eyes:
